key_insight: HiVLA preserves the high-level reasoning of large vision-language models by explicitly decoupling semantic planning from low-level motor control, using visual grounding as the bridge between the two. This hierarchical design keeps VLM reasoning intact while enabling robust, fine-grained manipulation.
problem_solved: End-to-end Vision–Language–Action fine-tuning often erodes the reasoning capabilities of base VLMs; HiVLA addresses the trade-off between preserving semantic reasoning and achieving precise motor control in embodied manipulation.
method: High-level VLM planner: uses vision-language models to perform semantic task decomposition and produce visually grounded subgoals (object parts, affordances, spatial relations).
Visual-grounding interface: maps semantic subgoals to image-space references and structured subtask representations that a controller can consume.
Modular low-level controller: separately trained motor policies (or classical controllers) execute grounded subgoals, allowing targeted fine-tuning without degrading VLM reasoning.
impact: HiVLA enables practitioners to combine strong VLM reasoning with reliable manipulation by modularizing planning and control, improving transferability, sample efficiency, and interpretability of robotic behaviors.
visual_elements: Two-tiered architecture diagram showing VLM planner → visual grounding layer → low-level controller with arrows and data types labeled.
Example task decomposition: input instruction + scene image → sequence of grounded subgoals overlaid on the image (object-part boxes, affordance icons).
Performance comparison chart: accuracy/success-rate or reasoning retention for HiVLA vs end-to-end VLA baselines across manipulation tasks.
Attention/grounding heatmaps on images to illustrate where the VLM focuses when generating subgoals.
paper_title: HiVLA: A Visual-Grounded-Centric Hierarchical Embodied Manipulation System
paper_authors: Tianshuo Yang, Guanyu Chen, Yutian Chen, Zhixuan Liang, Yitian Liu
